text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: Incident INC-2026-004 fired for service=redwood-serving-prod (high error rate). Trigger: 5xx spike on /v1/generate. Priority: P1. Escalation policy: default -> primary oncall -> secondary -> manager. Paging primary now.
pagerduty: Paging marta (primary) via phone and push. PD key: PD-xyz123. Details: avg 5xx rate 18% over 2m, latency p95 3.4s, customers seeing timeouts. Runbook: docs/runbooks/serving-5xx.md
marta: On it, waking up. Looking at dashboards.
marta: Checked k8s pods for serving cluster eu-west-1: a few restarts on model-worker-7. Pulling recent logs now.
ryan: (watching) If primary misses ack, PD will escalate to matt (secondary) after 2 minutes — heads up.
marta: I see repeated OOMs in model-worker-7 logs, memory spike right before restart. Heap growth in LM model process. Dumping stack and kube describe.
oncall-bot: matt is scheduled as secondary from 02:00-10:00 UTC today.
pm: matt: I just got a push. ACKING the incident so PD stops paging emergency contacts. I'll join.
matt: ack
pagerduty: Incident INC-2026-004 acknowledged by matt.
incident-bot: Note: primary (marta) did not acknowledge within 90s; escalation to secondary executed automatically. Manager escalation timer set to 8m if no resolution or no manual override.
ops-manager: I'm awake, logging in. If this is OOM-related, can we temporarily scale up memory on model-worker pool and restart gracefully?
ryan: Can we confirm whether this is correlated with a rollout? I see a deployment 15m ago that changed model shard config.
marta: I did a deploy rollback 10m ago automatically (canary failed) but some nodes still have new image. Rolling restart in progress to unify image to previous stable.
matt: While restart happens, I'll bump node memory requests to 48Gi for one replica to see if it prevents OOM and keeps traffic. Applying patch now:

```
kubectl patch deployment model-worker --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"model","resources":{"requests":{"memory":"48Gi"}}}]}}}}'
```

marta: Copy. Also enabling autoscale override to min 4 replicas to absorb burst.
oncall-bot: matt changed replicas to 4 (temp). Action: scale applied by ops playbook.
ryan: Observability: p95 latency dropping from 3.4s -> 1.2s on some routes, errors now 4% and trending down.
ops-manager: Good. Start notifying customers with incident status: investigating -> in progress -> mitigation started. Use status page link: status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-004
marta: Confirming: model-worker pod restarts stopped after scale/rollback. Root cause looks like memory regression in the new image's allocator for long sequences. Marking for postmortem.
matt: I'll monitor for 30 more minutes. If errors <1% and latency stable, we'll close and follow up with postmortem and rollback summary.
pagerduty: Incident INC-2026-004 status: mitigation in progress. Escalation policy paused by matt (secondary) at 1815554500.
incident-bot: Reminder: manager escalation window cancelled (ops-manager notified). Please add a short writeup in #postmortems when stable.
ryan: (reaction :thumbsup:) Great work team. Quick note: add the failing image tag to the rollback list.
ops-manager: Thanks — we'll schedule an eval with research/eng-ml to look at allocator change. For now, leave autoscale override for 1h then revert.
marta: Final check: traffic normalizing, no new OOMs. I'll sign off as primary once everything is green.
matt: I'll handback to marta in 10m if still green.
oncall-bot: Hand-off scheduled: matt -> marta at 1815555120.
incident-bot: Closing note: incident remains open until postmortem created. Update channel when you file it.
